CORAM:
 JUSTICE S.K. SAHOO  ORDER Order No. 18.09.2023  I.A. No.643 of 2021 10.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Video Conferencing/Physical Mode).
This is an application under section 389 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The appellant-petitioner, along with others, has been convicted for the offence punishable under section 376-D of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of twenty years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (rupees five thousand) and in default, to undergo further rigorous imprisonment for a further period of six months by the learned Addl.

Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, // 2 // Jharsuguda vide judgment dated 31.03.2021 in S.T.
Case No.90 of 2015.

Learned counsel for the State has produced the written instruction dated 05.08.2023 received from the Inspector in-charge of Banharpali police station from which it reveals that the victim has got married with another person and blessed with one male child and the petitioner has got no criminal antecedent.
The said written instruction is taken on record.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that out of twenty years of substantive sentence imposed by the learned trial Court, the petitioner has already undergone more than eight years and Ramakanta Naik vs State Of Odisha on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7559015/
1 two months of substantive sentence.

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submitted that even though the victim being examined within a few hours of the alleged rape, but the doctor did not find any spermatozoa inside her private part though she stated that spermatozoa normally disappears after twenty four hours and presence of spermatozoa is a positive sign of sexual intercourse.
The doctor has not mentioned the age of abrasion on the victim's private part and it is also not mentioned that the injuries were fresh.

The doctor further opined that the injuries on the victim are not possible through rape by three persons and it is only possible through rape by a single person and in case of forcible rape by three persons on a virgin girl, there // 3 // would be definitely profuse bleeding from her genital and she further stated that she did not notice any blood stain on the wearing apparels of the victim girl.

Learned counsel further argued that in view the evidence on record, the petitioner has good chances of success in the appeal, balance of convenience lies in his favour and this is an appeal of the year 2021 and since there is no chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, the bail application of the petitioner may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel for the State, on the other hand, opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that the victim's evidence is sufficient in itself to sustain the conviction of the petitioner.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, the nature of evidence adduced during trial, substantive sentence imposed by the learned trial court, the period already undergone by the petitioner in judicial custody and absence of any chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.

Let the appellant-petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of // 4 // the learned trial Court with such terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper.
The I.A. is disposed of.
( S.K. Sahoo) Judge 11.
This is an application for stay of realization of fine.
Heard.

There shall be stay of realization of fine amount imposed on the appellant-petitioner by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Judge, Jharsuguda vide judgment dated 31.03.2021 in S.T. Case No.90 of 2015 pending disposal of the criminal appeal.
The I.A. is disposed of.
Issue certified copy as per rules.
